title.en: Major record labels sue AI music generators Suno and Udio for copyright infringement
title.zhHans: 主要唱片公司起诉 AI 音乐生成器 Suno 和 Udio 侵犯版权

searchSummary.en: Major record labels sued AI music generators Suno and Udio in 2024 for copyright infringement. The legal battle that could decide the future of AI-generated music.
searchSummary.zhHans: 主要唱片公司 2024 年起诉 AI 音乐生成器 Suno 和 Udio 侵犯版权。这场诉讼可能决定 AI 生成音乐的未来。

summary.en: On June 24, 2024, the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA) filed two landmark copyright lawsuits against AI music generation companies Suno and Udio on behalf of Sony Music, Universal Music Group, and Warner Records. The suits alleged that the AI models were trained on copyrighted sound recordings without permission, and marked the first major legal confrontation between the music industry and generative AI. The cases set the template for AI x creative industry copyright disputes globally and led to partial settlements in 2025.
summary.zhHans: 2024 年 6 月 24 日，美国唱片业协会（RIAA）代表索尼音乐、环球音乐集团和华纳唱片对 AI 音乐生成公司 Suno 和 Udio 提起了两起里程碑式的版权诉讼。诉讼指控这些 AI 模型在未经许可的情况下使用受版权保护的音乐录音进行训练，标志着音乐产业与生成式 AI 之间的首次重大法律对抗。这些案件为全球 AI 与创意产业版权纠纷设定了模板，并在 2025 年促成了部分和解。

narrative.en: The lawsuits came after a year of explosive growth in AI music generation. Suno and Udio, both launched in 2023-2024, could generate convincing songs from text prompts — complete with vocals, lyrics, and instrumentation in any genre. The technology was so good that generated songs went viral, raising immediate alarm in the record industry. The RIAA's lawsuits were sweeping: they alleged that the AI models had been trained on 'vast swaths' of copyrighted music, including works from artists like Taylor Swift, The Beatles, and Drake. The cases highlighted a fundamental tension that would define AI copyright debates: is training an AI on copyrighted material fair use (as AI companies argued) or infringement (as creators argued)? Suno and Udio took different legal strategies: Suno initially fought the case, while Udio engaged in settlement talks earlier. By late 2025, Universal Music Group settled with Udio, and Warner Music Group reached settlements with both companies. The cases, alongside the NYT v. OpenAI lawsuit, established 2024 as the year the legal framework for generative AI training data began to take shape. The music industry lawsuits particularly resonated because AI-generated music directly threatened the economic model of the recording industry in a way that text generation did not for publishers.
narrative.zhHans: 这些诉讼发生在 AI 音乐生成爆发式增长一年之后。Suno 和 Udio 都在 2023-2024 年推出，能够从文本提示生成令人信服的歌曲——包括人声、歌词和任何流派的编曲。这项技术的质量如此之高，以至于生成的歌曲在网上病毒式传播，立即引起了唱片业的警觉。RIAA 的诉讼影响深远：他们指控这些 AI 模型使用了"大量"受版权保护的音乐进行训练，包括 Taylor Swift、The Beatles 和 Drake 等艺术家的作品。这些案件凸显了将定义 AI 版权辩论的一个根本性紧张关系：在受版权保护的材料上训练 AI 是合理使用（如 AI 公司所主张）还是侵权（如创作者所主张）？Suno 和 Udio 采取了不同的法律策略：Suno 最初积极抗辩，而 Udio 更早参与和解谈判。到 2025 年底，环球音乐集团与 Udio 达成和解，华纳音乐集团与两家公司都达成了和解。这些案件与 NYT 诉 OpenAI 案一起，将 2024 年确立为生成式 AI 训练数据法律框架开始成形的年份。音乐产业诉讼之所以特别引人共鸣，是因为 AI 生成的音乐以文本生成对出版商所没有的方式直接威胁了唱片业的经济模式。

description.en: Threatened the economic model of the recording industry by enabling AI-generated music that competes with human-created songs. The lawsuits became a template for how creative industries could defend their intellectual property against generative AI. Partial settlements in 2025 began establishing licensing norms for AI training data in music.
description.zhHans: 通过使 AI 生成的音乐与人类创作的歌曲竞争，威胁了唱片业的经济模式。这些诉讼成为创意产业如何捍卫其知识产权对抗生成式 AI 的模板。2025 年的部分和解开始为音乐领域的 AI 训练数据建立授权规范。

description.en: Created legal uncertainty for the entire AI music generation sector. Raised questions about whether AI training on copyright-protected creative works is fair use or infringement — a question that remains unresolved.
description.zhHans: 为整个 AI 音乐生成领域带来了法律不确定性。提出了在受版权保护的创意作品上训练 AI 是合理使用还是侵权的问题——这个问题至今未解。

text.en: The RIAA filed copyright infringement lawsuits against Suno and Udio on June 24, 2024, on behalf of Sony Music, Universal Music Group, and Warner Records.
text.zhHans: RIAA 于 2024 年 6 月 24 日代表索尼音乐、环球音乐集团和华纳唱片对 Suno 和 Udio 提起版权侵权诉讼。

sources.quote: Record Companies Bring Landmark Cases for Responsible AI Against Suno and Udio in Boston and New York Federal Courts.
Music labels sue AI song generators Suno and Udio for copyright infringement.
